summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 66% to Rs.319.6 Crores with PAT margin of 12.2%; FY27 guidance is Rs.500 Crores revenue at 12-13% PAT margin.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs.319.6 Crores (up 66% YoY), with H2 contributing Rs.229.1 Crores (up 114% YoY), and EBITDA of Rs.64.2 Crores at a 20.1% margin (EBITDA margin down from about 25% per analyst question). PAT was Rs.39.1 Crores (up 52%) at a 12.2% margin. Management said the Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly because it declined to pursue low-margin re-tenders amid aluminium and stainless steel inflation. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs.500 Crores at 12-13% PAT margin, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure varied in the call) and a Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs Rs.192.4 Crores in FY25
+114% YoY vs Rs.107.3 Crores in H2 FY25
receivable days down 24 days; inventory days down 48 days

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver; management says about 70% of the pipeline is railway, roughly Rs.900 Crores of the Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline, covering Atmanirbhar Bharat, Spark and Kavach coaches, Vande Bharat sleeper and Amrit Bharat turnkey contracts. Refurbishment is cited as a separate opportunity of about Rs.26,000 Crores sanctioned, with hoped-for orders of at least Rs.100 Crores this year.

segments.name: Metro
segments.commentary: About Rs.70 Crores of metro orders held, with another Rs.120 Crores expected within the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline; Kolkata Metro turnkey contracts are named as a focus.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Rs.29 Crores of current order book to execute this year, plus Rs.60-70 Crores expected from HAL tenders (mainly simulators, not AMCA airframe production). Proposed JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions to be incorporated before 15 June 2026; Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores, focused on autonomous drones and electronic warfare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of approximately Rs.500 Crores with PAT margin of 12-13%; management said PAT would not fall below 12%.
Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly; management also said it could be reached in FY28 or earlier if conditions allow.
Management said about 70-75% of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.
R&D spend to rise to about 8-9% of sales this year from about 4% earlier; management later said R&D spend would be capitalised on the balance sheet.
Capex of Rs.30-40 Crores planned for FY27-28, including about Rs.30-35 Crores for a 14-acre facility with 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft of initial shed space, expanding to 3-4 lakh sq ft.
Debt funding of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% from two banks: Rs.60 Crores sanctioned, the other Rs.60 Crores expected by end June 2026. No equity raise planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation is about 90% of existing facility; two-shift operations in use since around December 2025.
New 14-acre facility planned: initial 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft, later extending to 3-4 lakh sq ft; land already acquired and term loan discussions with bankers under way.

Machinery purchases, mostly from China, delayed because Chinese OEMs require an end-user certificate from the Government of India; management expected clarity in June 2026 and may switch to different machinery for lightweight rail interiors.
Plans to consolidate seven units into about two, reducing rent of roughly Rs.20-25 lakh per month.
Channel partner model in place to execute zonal railway contracts without building facilities in each region.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure cited differently in different answers): Rs.415-420 Crores government and Rs.50-55 Crores non-government.
Bid pipeline about Rs.1,200 Crores with historical bid-win ratio of about 20-25%.

Raw material inflation: aluminium up more than 80% and stainless steel up 60-65% YoY; price variation clauses cover only about 50-60% of the increase, and accessories (30-35% of assembly cost) are not covered.
Competitors named: Kineco, Hindustan Fiberglass Works, DTL Ancillaries, Vibgyor, Universal Engineers; seating competitors Tata (with Fainsa), a Korean firm and firms from Mumbai and Bengaluru.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end; receivable and working capital cycles targeted at 60-70 days from 90-95 days within 3-4 months. Debt of Rs.120 Crores is being raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure and its causes in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium and stainless steel inflation hit margins. Management said price variation covers only about 50-60% of losses, and it used advances, LCs and BGs to block vendor prices, limiting losses to 20-25% of the uncovered amount.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of added debt interest and R&D on the 12-13% PAT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would stay at or above 12%, citing higher-margin bids and that R&D spend would be deployed only when expected returns are met.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 revenue reach Rs.1,000 Crores and PAT Rs.150 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and that FY28 could exceed Rs.1,000 Crores, without firm numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.500 Crores target hold given 90% utilisation and machinery delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery delays would not affect FY27 turnover; two-shift operation and channel partners could add Rs.400-450 Crores from the Rs.320 Crores base.

risks_watch: Working capital: trade receivables of Rs.214 Crores at year-end; collection of about 70% expected by June, and cash conversion still negative.
Debt servicing: about Rs.120 Crores new debt at 8.25% adds interest cost of roughly Rs.10 Crores per year, per the analyst's calculation.
Raw material and commodity inflation, with price variation clauses covering only part of the increase.
Dependence on lumpy Indian Railways orders and back-loaded execution in H2.
Possible equity raise in FY28, which management did not rule out.
Defence revenue timing: management said defence products need 6-12 months of trials, and the Big Bang Boom JV is expected to be incorporated before 15 June 2026.
Inconsistent figures on order book (Rs.469 Crores vs Rs.486.9 Crores) and on EBITDA margin, which the analyst described as falling from 25% to 20%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 execution and margins, but evasive on timing for the Rs.1,000 Crores milestone and on defence revenue, which management described as a long-cycle, first-time bid area. Several answers were repetitive or unclear, and management did not give firm numbers for the JV or the new facility.
key_quotes: Looking ahead, we are targeting a revenue of approximately Rs.500 Crores in FY 2027 while maintaining PAT margin in the range between 12% to 13%.
So I do not think that we can reduce our overall PAT level less than 12% for sure.
The bidding of Rs.1200 Crores is predominantly on the Indian railway sector.
